bio.en: Jonny Miller is a coach and educator who created Nervous System Mastery, a program that teaches tech professionals practical tools to build calm, resilience, and sustained high performance.
bio.zh: 乔尼·米勒（Jonny Miller）是一位教练与教育工作者，他创立了"神经系统掌控力"（Nervous System Mastery）项目，向科技从业者传授培养内心平静、提升抗压能力与持续高效状态的实用工具。

summary.en: Jonny shares his "feather, brick, dump truck" framework, which shows that burnout begins with subtle bodily signals that escalate into crises if ignored. He argues that learning to notice early feedback lets people course-correct long before a breakdown. The conversation offers concrete techniques for regulating the nervous system, reframing burnout prevention as a trainable, body-based skill.
summary.zh: 乔尼提出了"羽毛、砖头、自卸卡车"框架，说明职业倦怠往往从细微的身体信号开始，若被忽视便会升级为危机。他认为，学会捕捉早期的反馈，能让人在彻底崩溃前及时调整方向。本期还分享了许多调节神经系统的具体方法，把预防倦怠重新定义为一种可以通过训练获得的、基于身体的能力。

turns.speaker: Jonny Miller
turns.en: I have this idea that I call the feather brick dump truck phenomenon, and basically what that means is when we are showing early signs of burnout, our body will give us feedback usually in subtle ways in the beginning. So the feather might be waking up in the morning and feeling a little bit tired, maybe a little bit exhausted. The brick, maybe you ignore that or you don't notice it, and then three or four weeks later, you have a fight with someone or an argument, or you just feel frustrated and terrible and you lose your cool. And then maybe the dump truck is a month later, or even a year later, there's a full-blown health crisis, or you develop type two diabetes or there's a whole range of things, or maybe you get fired. Ideally, you want to notice when it's the feather and then make adjustments or shift then and not have to wait until you experience the full-blown pain of the dump truck, which unfortunately is what happens to a lot of people, especially when they experience burnout for the first time.
turns.zh: 我有个概念，叫“羽毛砖倾卸卡车现象”。简单来说，当我们出现职业倦怠的早期征兆时，身体通常会以微妙的方式给出反馈。比如“羽毛”阶段，早上醒来可能会感到有些疲倦，或许还有些精疲力竭。而“砖块”阶段，你或许会忽视这些信号，或者没有注意到它们。三四周后，你可能会和别人发生冲突、争吵，或者陷入情绪低落、情绪崩溃的状态。再过一个月、甚至一年，可能就会爆发严重的健康危机，比如患上二型糖尿病，或者遭遇一系列其他问题。理想情况下，你应该在“羽毛”阶段就察觉到问题并及时调整，而不是等到“倾卸卡车”阶段才亡羊补牢。遗憾的是，大多数人往往都是到了“倾卸卡车”阶段才意识到问题的严重性，尤其是那些初次经历职业倦怠的人。

I find that usually people that get into this type of work, there's some kind of catalyst or some kind of challenging life event. turns.speaker: Jonny Miller
turns.en: So I find this top down, bottom up distinction to be incredibly helpful. Most people when they try to calm down, they use tactical reframes or maybe mindfulness or maybe reframing the situation in a positive light. There's lots of different practices that people use which do have some effect. But in my experience, working with the physiology, using what's known as a bottom up approach, primarily using the breath, although there's also other approaches that you can use, it's just such a rapidly more effective way of shifting your state. (00:08:11): And to give a little bit of context and maybe some science as well, we have what's known as afferent and efferent neurons going up and down our body, and there's four times more afferent neurons going from the body to the brain as from the brain to the body. So you can almost imagine there's a super highway of traffic of information going up to the brain and four times less going from the brain to the body. And so by learning how to pull on the levers of our physiology, we can rapidly change our state. And then from there, by changing our state, that impacts the thoughts and feelings that we have. So instead of trying to change the story or trying to fix something or trying to solve something, which is what most people do by default, myself included in the past, if you change your state first, then there's a cascading effect which changes your thoughts and your feelings.
turns.zh: 因此，我发现这种自上而下、自下而上的区分非常有用。大多数人在试图平静下来时，会使用战术性的重新构建思维方式，或许会尝试正念，或许会以积极的视角重新审视处境。人们使用的各种方法确实能产生一些效果。但以我的经验来看，从生理层面入手，采用所谓自下而上的方法，主要通过呼吸来调整状态，这种方法能更迅速地改变情绪状态。（00:08:11） 先讲点背景知识和科学原理。我们的身体里有传入神经和传出神经，它们像高速公路一样在体内来回传递信息。从身体到大脑的传入神经数量是大脑到身体的四倍。所以可以想象，有一条信息高速公路从身体传向大脑，而从大脑传向身体的信息却少得多。因此，通过学习如何调控生理机制，我们能迅速改变自身状态。进而，通过改变状态，影响我们的思维和情绪。与大多数人（包括过去的我）习惯先试图改变事件经过、解决问题或修正现状不同，如果先调整自身状态，随后就会引发连锁反应，进而改变思维和情绪。

If you start breathing into your upper chest and shallow fairly, fairly rapid, maybe even through the mouth, that will then there's a part of your brain called the insular cortex, which is basically constantly spying on the way that we're breathing and it will register that change, it will then send information to activate the endocrine system, which then creates shift in our blood chemistry. The sympathetic nervous system gets activated and that increase in adrenaline and cortisol starts to flood your body. Everyone's probably very familiar with that feeling. And then that will then have a cascading impact on the thoughts that you're having and the way that you feel. And so you just shared, we have a tendency to kind of confabulate or make up stories that match the state that we are in. And so that's kind of what happens when we're breathing in that way. And then you can also consciously change your breath to breathe in a different way, which has the reverse effects, which I can go into, but I'll pause there.
turns.zh: 我的意思是，我认为理解这个过程很有帮助。比如，通过改变呼吸方式，我们就能改变生理状态，调节神经系统。如果你正在听这段讲话，也许你，莱尼，你也可以试试看。如果你开始用胸部上部浅而快速地呼吸，甚至可能通过嘴巴呼吸，那么大脑中一个叫做岛叶皮层的区域就会不断监测我们的呼吸方式，感知到这种变化后，会向内分泌系统发送信号，进而改变我们的血液化学成分。交感神经系统被激活，肾上腺素和皮质醇水平升高，整个身体会产生应激反应。大家对这种感觉应该很熟悉。随后，呼吸方式的改变会对我们的思维和情绪产生连锁反应。正如你刚才提到的，我们往往会编造故事来迎合当时的情绪状态，而这种呼吸方式恰恰会引发这种现象。当然，你也可以有意识地调整呼吸方式，产生相反的效果——这部分我可以详细讲解，但现在先暂停。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: You also have this really clever way of describing this system. You call it state over story, essentially focusing on the state of your body versus the story you're telling yourself. Is that the way to think about it? And can you just talk about that concept?
turns.zh: 你还用了一个非常巧妙的方式来描述这个系统。你称之为"状态优先于故事"，本质上是关注身体状态而非我们给自己编造的故事。是这样理解的吗？你能谈谈这个概念吗？

turns.speaker: Jonny Miller
turns.en: Yeah, so it's basically a shorthand for what we've just been talking about, which is most people tend to approach the problem or try to solve things on the level of story. So there's multiple ways you can do that through the breath as we just talked about. You can also defocus your gaze and kind of relax your eyes, and that has a similar effect. It can expand your awareness and kind of bring your awareness to behind you and the sides of you and below you, or you can breathe in these ways which emphasize the exhale. And so when we breathe in a way with say the exhale twice as long as the inhale, that part of the brain, the insular cortex then sends signals to the parasympathetic nervous system, which then has the cascading effect on our endocrine system and calms us down. And what I usually find as well is that the kind of reactive thoughts and feelings that we have when we are in that kind of anxious loop, they can be self-reinforcing. And so if someone has a thought of like, "Oh no, I'm nervous before this important presentation." Then that exacerbates the breathing pattern and then the whole thing just goes into this spiral, which can end up in full-blown panic attacks if there's not an intervention of some sorts.
turns.zh: 是的，这基本上就是我们刚刚讨论的内容的简称——大多数人倾向于从故事的层面来处理问题或试图解决难题。正如我们刚刚提到的，可以通过呼吸来实现这一目标。你也可以让视线模糊，放松眼睛，这会有类似的效果。它能扩展你的意识范围，让你的注意力转向身后、侧面和下方。或者你可以通过强调呼气的方式呼吸。当我们以吸气两次，呼气一次的比例呼吸时，脑岛皮层会向副交感神经系统发送信号，从而对内分泌系统产生连锁反应，让我们平静下来。我还发现，当我们陷入焦虑循环时，那些反应性思维和情绪会自我强化。比如有人会想：“天啊，我要在重要演讲前紧张了。”这会加剧呼吸模式，整个循环可能会演变成全面的恐慌发作，除非采取某种干预措施。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Yeah, that's what I find with my nerves. I hate talking on stage. I get nervous before every podcast. This is not my natural state.
turns.zh: 是啊，我对自己紧张这事深有体会。我讨厌在台上演讲。每次做播客前我都会紧张。这根本不是我的自然状态。

turns.speaker: Jonny Miller
turns.en: Interesting.
turns.zh: 真有意思。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Yeah, and I hide it well.
turns.zh: 是啊，我掩饰得很到位。

turns.speaker: Jonny Miller
turns.en: Is that still the case with podcast today?
turns.zh: 那你现在做播客时还是这样吗？

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Absolutely. And it's like different levels of nervousness, but it's always just like, "Oh, there we go." I'm not a performer person. Even I kind of push myself to do this podcast as a way to get better at this, to be honest. So it's still a thing that I think about. And what I find is the nervousness comes from exactly what you described is the nervousness of being nervous. I don't know, there's no reason specifically to be anxious, but I don't know how I'll be once I do the thing. So it's nervous of what it might look like or end up being like. So that's exactly what I ran into.
turns.zh: 当然了。紧张程度不同，但总会出现那种“哦，糟糕”的感觉。我不是个善于表演的人，说实话，我强迫自己做播客，就是为了在这方面有所提升。所以这事儿我一直挂念在心。我发现紧张源自你所描述的对紧张本身的紧张。我不知道为什么会焦虑，但又不知道做完事后自己会表现成什么样。所以就是对可能呈现出的结果感到紧张。这正是我遇到的困境。

turns.speaker: Jonny Miller
turns.en: Yeah. And there's obviously people say mindfulness, meditation, things like that, that can increase the psychological space between stimulus and response. And that is something that obviously does help over the long term, but it's in my opinion, nowhere near as rapid and effective and efficient as just changing the way that you're breathing.
turns.zh: 是啊。有的人提到正念、冥想之类的方法，能增加刺激与反应之间的心理空间。从长远来看，这确实有帮助，但在我看来，远不如改变呼吸方式来得迅速、有效和高效。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Awesome. So let's get into it. I know you have a couple exercises specifically for this, and then we'll go from there.
turns.zh: 太棒了。那我们开始吧。我知道你有几个专门针对这个的练习，接下来我们就按步骤来。

turns.speaker: Jonny Miller
turns.en: We can stack a few of the exercises and I'll try and keep it to a minute or so. So yeah, if you want to get comfy in your chair and sit up straight, feel your butt on the seat, and I find it helpful to kind of be aware of the space behind you and above you as well, kind of expanding your awareness so that you are aware of the space behind to the sides and above.
turns.zh: 我们可以把几个练习组合起来，每次控制在一分钟左右。首先，你可以舒服地坐在椅子上，挺直腰板，感觉到屁股坐在座位上。我发现把注意力放在身后和头顶的空间也很有帮助，这样能扩展你的意识范围，让你意识到身后、侧面和上方的空间。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: And should we close your eyes?
turns.zh: 那我们要闭上眼睛吗？

turns.speaker: Jonny Miller
turns.en: Yeah, and close your eyes down. If you're listening and driving, obviously don't do that. But yeah, closing the eyes down for sure helps. And now we're just going to do simple breath. We're going to inhale in through the nose for four. We're going to hold the breath at the top for four, and we're going to exhale for eight, and then we're going to repeat. So let the breath go and inhaling through the nose. Inhale, 2, 3, 4, hold the breath, 2, 3, 4. And exhale, 8, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8. Inhale, 2, 3, 4, hold the breath, 2, 3, 4, and exhale, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8. And now you can let go of the breath completely and we'll end with one round of humming, which is surprisingly effect of it calming as well. So take a full breath in and humming through the nose all the way to the end of exhale. Let out a sigh if that feels good and open up your eyes.
turns.zh: 是的，还有闭上眼睛。如果你正在开车听播客，显然不能这样做。不过闭上眼睛确实有帮助。现在我们要进行简单的呼吸练习。先用鼻子吸气四秒，屏住呼吸四秒，再用口呼气八秒，接着重复一次。先让气息自然流出，用鼻子吸气，再吸气2、3、4秒，屏住呼吸2、3、4秒，呼气8、2、3、4、5、6、7秒。接着吸气2、3、4秒，屏住呼吸2、3、4秒，呼气2、3、4、5、6、7秒。最后彻底呼出气息，结束时我们再进行一轮哼唱练习，效果出奇地令人平静。所以深吸一口气，用鼻子哼唱，持续到呼气结束。感觉好的时候可以叹口气，睁开眼睛。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: I feel extremely calm. I should do this every podcast episode before we start.
turns.zh: 我感觉非常平静。每次播客开场前我都应该这么做。

turns.speaker: Jonny Miller
turns.en: A note on the humming. It also releases nitric oxide, which is a vasodilator, and that helps to create that kind of calming effect and it also reduces eye tension as well. So I'll do it if I've been looking to screen for too long. It's really good for kind of reducing eye fatigue as well.
turns.zh: 关于哼唱的注意事项。它还能释放一氧化氮，这是一种血管扩张剂，有助于缓解紧张情绪，还能缓解眼部疲劳。所以当我看屏幕太久时，就会这么做。它对缓解眼疲劳也很有效。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: And there's also a vagus nerve component to it because your body's vibrating, is that true?
turns.zh: 还有迷走神经的成分，因为身体在振动，对吧？

turns.speaker: Jonny Miller
turns.en: Yeah, precisely. So it kind of tones or stimulates the vagus nerve, which stimulates the parasympathetic nervous system.
turns.zh: 是的，没错。所以它能调节或刺激迷走神经，进而刺激副交感神经系统。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: What's your advice for doing this? Is this before you go into a big meeting or a presentation? How do you apply this?
turns.zh: 你对此有什么建议吗？是在参加重要会议或演讲前做准备吗？如何应用这些方法？

turns.speaker: Jonny Miller
turns.en: I kind of like to share building a toolkit of different practices that are appropriate for different contexts. So something like the 4, 4, 8 breathing, you could do pretty much anywhere without anyone necessarily noticing. Humming is slightly more obvious, but if you're about to jump on a zoom or something, you can totally do it with your eyes closed. Things like expanding your awareness or bringing your awareness down to your feet and your hands, which creates a kind of grounding calming effect that also you can do if you're in a busy room. Maybe you have social anxiety, even orienting and labeling things that you are hearing and feeling, kind of bringing the awareness and attention back into the body that also has an effect. And then there's longer practices for say, non-sleep deep rests, belly breathing, things that you can do if you have 10, 20 minutes and you're at home and you want a downshift. (00:18:30): So I like to kind of give people a big toolkit to see what works for them and then cherry-pick which ones are suitable to different situations. And another way that I think about this is, I call it, if this, then breathe. So it's like if I feel overwhelmed, then I do the humming. If I feel anxious, then I do 4, 4, 8 breathing or alternate nostril breathing and kind of having my own little recipe set that I have for different context is really helpful and I work with people to kind of build those toolkits themselves.
turns.zh: 我比较喜欢分享适合不同场景的不同练习工具箱。比如4秒、4秒、8秒呼吸法，你几乎可以在任何地方做，别人不会注意到。哼唱稍微明显一些，但如果你要参加视频会议之类的，闭着眼睛完全没问题。还有扩展意识或将注意力转移到脚和手上，这能带来接地气的平静效果，尤其是在繁忙的房间里也很适用。甚至对于社交焦虑的人，通过感知和标注听到和感受到的东西，将注意力引回身体，也有效果。然后还有更长时间的练习，比如非睡眠深度休息、腹式呼吸等，如果你有10、20分钟时间在家想放松一下，都可以尝试。（00:18:30）所以我喜欢给人们一个大工具箱，让他们看看哪些方法适合自己，然后根据不同情况灵活选择。另外，我常用的方法是，如果出现这种情况，就呼吸。比如如果我感到不知所措，就进行哼唱。如果感到焦虑，就进行4秒、4秒、8秒呼吸法或交替鼻孔呼吸法。为不同场景制定自己的小习惯真的很有帮助，我也会帮助人们自己建立这样的工具箱。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: This sounds like it needs to be a website where people can go with these lists of if this, then that is there a place that we could send people in the show notes and if not, you should make one before we go live.
turns.zh: 这听起来需要一个网站，让人们能获取这些“如果这样，就呼吸”的清单。节目笔记里有没有相关链接？如果没有，建议在直播前搭建一个。

turns.speaker: Jonny Miller
turns.en: There is not currently. It's part of the curriculum in the course that I have, but-
turns.zh: 目前还没有。这是我所授课程的教学内容之一，不过——

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Okay, great.
turns.zh: 好的，太棒了。

turns.speaker: Jonny Miller
turns.en: ... I can maybe see if I can spin one up as well, but yeah.
turns.zh: ……或许我可以看看能否也开设一个相关课程，不过确实。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Okay, cool. We'll link to the course if nothing else. Amazing.
turns.zh: 好的，没问题。如果没别的办法，我们就直接链接到课程页面吧。这太棒了。

turns.speaker: Jonny Miller
turns.en: Okay.
turns.zh: 好的。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Along this line of calming breath exercise, Huberman also has a different version, which I've tried and I'm going to do both now. You breathe in fully and then you breathe in a little bit more. I imagine you've seen that piece of advice?
turns.zh: 关于这种平静呼吸练习，胡贝尔曼还有另一种版本，我试过，现在两种方法都会用。一吸气，再稍微多吸一点。我想你们应该见过这个建议吧？

turns.speaker: Jonny Miller
turns.en: That's also fantastic. He calls it the physiological sigh, and it's both very effective, especially if you just have five seconds and you just take a full sigh, it's great. I'd also add that the sigh happens naturally as a result of doing these downshifting practices. So if you notice after you do let's say the 4, 4, 8 breathing, at the end, you might naturally just want to let out a sigh, and that's a signal that your body is naturally downshifting. Or if you are with a friend and you feel just comfortable and relaxed, then your body might sigh. And it's something that we do a lot and as you say, you can consciously do it and that will help as well. That's another one of the practices.
turns.zh: 那也很棒。他称之为"生理叹息"，效果非常显著，尤其是当你只有五秒钟时间，就深吸一口气，再呼出来，效果绝佳。我还要补充一点，这种叹息是自然发生的，源于这些减压练习。所以如果你完成比如4、4、8呼吸法后，最后可能就会自然地叹口气，这表明你的身体正在自然地减压。或者如果你和朋友在一起，感觉非常舒适放松，身体也会叹气。这种情况我们经常遇到，正如你所说，你可以有意识地去做，这也很有帮助。这也是一种练习方法。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Awesome. So link to that. And I think throughout this episode, as you said, we're going to give people a bunch of tools that they can use, and it feels like some are in the moment, "I need to feel calmer right now. Here's a thing you could do." And then there's things you can do ongoing that build... I guess another way to think about it's just make your body more calm as a baseline of practice to work on there.
turns.zh: 太棒了。那就把链接发给大家吧。我觉得在这一期节目中，正如你所说，我们会给人们提供一系列可以运用的工具，有些是即时应对的，比如“我现在需要冷静下来，可以试试这个方法”。还有一些是持续练习的，能逐渐培养……换个角度想，就是让身体保持更平静的基准状态，然后再在此基础上努力。

turns.speaker: Jonny Miller
turns.en: Yeah, precisely.
turns.zh: 对，完全正确。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Awesome, okay. I think the other breathing exercise we're going to do is the opposite. Gets you all excited, is that right?
turns.zh: 太棒了，好的。我想我们要做的另一个呼吸练习正好相反，能让你兴奋起来，对吧？

turns.speaker: Jonny Miller
turns.en: Yeah, sure. We can do that as well. I call this espresso breath. So this is the opposite. This is very activating. I would only recommend this if you're feeling lethargic or maybe instead of drinking a coffee in the afternoon, you could do this for a minute or so. In the scientific literature, it's bellows breath or breath of fire, and it basically looks like a series of rapid exhales through the nose. I like to keep it through the nose only if you do it through the mouth, it can be very too activating and it can kind of overwhelm people. Obviously, there's the Wim Hof practice that I'm sure many people are familiar with. So this is a more gentle version of... If Wim Hof is like Red Bull, this is kind of like a small coffee.
turns.zh: 对，没错。我们也可以试试这个。我把它叫做“意式浓缩呼吸法”。所以这完全相反。非常激活身心。我只建议在感觉困倦时使用，或者下午不想喝咖啡时，可以试试这个动作，持续一分钟左右。在科学文献中，这叫做“风箱呼吸”或“火焰呼吸”，基本上就是通过鼻子快速呼气。只要通过鼻子呼吸就行，如果用嘴呼吸，可能太兴奋了，会让人应接不暇。显然，很多人都熟悉维姆·霍夫的呼吸法。所以这是一个更温和的版本……如果维姆·霍夫是红牛，那这个就相当于一杯小咖啡。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: I like that. And you call it the espresso breath, espresso breath.
turns.zh: 我喜欢这个说法。就叫它意式浓缩呼吸法吧，意式浓缩呼吸法。

turns.speaker: Jonny Miller
turns.en: Espresso breath, yeah.
turns.zh: 意式浓缩呼吸法，对。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: So yeah, that's a good metaphor there.
turns.zh: 所以是的，这个比喻很贴切。

turns.speaker: Jonny Miller
turns.en: Yeah, yeah. So yeah, let's do it. So again, kind of sit up straight, and this time you want to be pumping the breath from your lower belly and you pump the breath on the exhale. So I'll demonstrate it briefly. It's like breathe in. (00:21:56): Okay. So yeah, take a full breath in and begin. (00:21:58): And let go. And full breath in. And sigh on the exhale. I already feel a little bit tingly.
turns.zh: 是啊，是啊。所以好吧，我们开始吧。还是要坐直了，这次你要从下腹部吸气，然后呼气时把气呼出来。让我简单示范一下。吸气的时候（00:21:56）：好的。所以深吸一口气，然后开始。（00:21:58）：然后放松。再深吸一口气，然后呼气时叹口气。我已经感觉有点发麻了。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: I'm energized. Let's do this. Go, go, go, go. That was great. Okay, look at that. We're back to where we started with the full circle of energy. That was great.
turns.zh: 我现在充满活力。让我们继续吧。加油，加油，加油，加油。太棒了。好的，看看这里。我们又回到了能量循环的起点。太棒了。

turns.speaker: Jonny Miller
turns.en: Up and down.
turns.zh: 上上下下。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: And then how long do you recommend doing that one for?
turns.zh: 那你建议一次做多久呢？

turns.speaker: Jonny Miller
turns.en: So it kind of depends on how activating you find it, but I usually find 30 breaths per round and then take a breath, have a long pause on the exhale, and then if you want to do another round or two.
turns.zh: 这取决于你觉得它有多提神，但我通常一次30次呼吸，然后休息一会儿，再做一轮或两轮。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Amazing. And the cases where this might be helpful is maybe you're about to give a big talk, I guess in a talk you both want energy and want calm, so that's kind of complicated.
turns.zh: 太棒了。这种情况下可能会有帮助的，比如你即将要做一个重要的演讲，我猜你既想要活力又想要冷静，所以这有点矛盾。

turns.speaker: Jonny Miller
turns.en: Especially if you are meetings early in the morning and you haven't quite got going yet, you can do the espresso breath to begin with and that activates you. And then do some of the downshifting practices to kind of ground and stabilize that aliveness.
turns.zh: 特别是如果你早上开会还没完全进入状态，你可以先做一下“浓缩咖啡呼吸法”来提神，然后再做一些放松练习来稳定这种活力。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Are there any other tactical breathing exercises that are worth doing real quick? I know we'll get into some longer practices and deeper stuff, but is there anything else that would be helpful here?
turns.zh: 还有其他快速有效的呼吸练习吗？我知道我们后面会讲更深入的内容，但现在有没有什么值得快速尝试的？

turns.speaker: Jonny Miller
turns.en: No, I think we've covered the bases. I don't want to overwhelm people too much.
turns.zh: 不，我觉得我们已经讲到重点了。我不想让大家觉得负担太重。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Just as a takeaway, there's these two techniques. One to help you get more calm when you need to be calm in the moment. The other is to get energy. And then I guess are these things that you recommend doing ongoing to build this muscle in your body or are these mostly for you need this now in the moment and it's not worth just doing a few times a day even when you're fine?
turns.zh: 总结一下，就是这两个技巧。一个是在你需要冷静的时候帮助你保持冷静。另一个是获取能量。那么这些技巧是建议大家持续练习来锻炼身体，还是只在当下需要时用几次呢？

turns.speaker: Jonny Miller
turns.en: Yeah, great question. So I like to recommend both a morning practice, particularly to build the muscle of just doing it and getting used to it. So maybe five minutes in the morning before you start work, before breakfast, something like that. And then you are more likely to remember that you have access to that in the moment because usually the challenge is that when someone is in that flustered state, remembering to do the practice is often the last thing that comes to mind. So by having a deliberate practice for at least 7 to 10 days and so that you get the hang of it, then it feels much more natural to do it when you're feeling. That's kind of like playing the game on hard mode when you are really stressed and anxious, that's when you need it the most, but it's also when you're least likely to remember to do it.
turns.zh: 是的，问得好。我建议早上练习，尤其是为了养成习惯。比如早上五分钟，在开始工作前、吃早餐前之类的。这样你更有可能在需要时记住这些技巧，因为通常当人处于慌乱状态时，想起练习往往是最后才想到的。所以通过至少7到10天的刻意练习，让你掌握这些技巧，这样当你真正需要时，做起来就会自然得多。这就像在你压力大、焦虑时，游戏难度调到最高级别一样，那时你最需要它，但也最容易忘记去做。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Awesome. Okay, so the first exercise to calm you down is essentially breathe in four seconds, hold it for four seconds, breathe out slowly for eight seconds and do that for about 30 seconds, is that right? Or for a minute?
turns.zh: 太棒了。好的，第一个冷静练习基本上是吸气四秒，停四秒，慢慢呼气八秒，重复30秒，对吗？或者一分钟？

turns.speaker: Jonny Miller
turns.en: Yeah, I'd say for at least a minute or two. We kind of did a shorter version. I'll also add that the important thing is that the exhale is twice as long as the inhale. So if exhaling for eight is too long, you could do 3, 3, 6 or even 2, 2, 4 or even 5, 5, 10 depending on your lung capacity essentially and your CO2 tolerance.
turns.zh: 是啊，我觉得至少要坚持一两分钟。我们做了一个简化版的。另外需要强调的是，呼气的时间要比吸气长一倍。比如，如果八秒的呼气太长，你可以调整为3、3、6秒，甚至2、2、4秒，或者5、5、10秒，这取决于你的肺活量和二氧化碳耐受能力。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Okay, good to know. And then the espresso breath, when you need energy or you just kind of pump air out of your belly through your nose and you do that for how long would you recommend?
turns.zh: 好的，明白了。那关于浓缩咖啡呼吸法，当你需要提神，或者只是想把腹部积压的空气通过鼻子排出时，建议保持多久呢？

turns.speaker: Jonny Miller
turns.en: Two to three rounds of 30 pumps, yeah.
turns.zh: 两到三轮，每轮30次。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: And again, the reason this is effective and powerful is coming back to your original big insight that our state is driven by what our body is doing and our mind often explains what we're feeling based on what our body's doing. So that if you can change the state of your body and become less nervous in your body, your mind will be like, "All right, everything's fine."
turns.zh: 再说回来，之所以这种方法有效且强大，源于你最初提到的核心观点：我们的情绪状态是由身体的生理反应驱动的，而大脑往往会根据身体的状态来解读我们的感受。因此，如果你能改变身体的状态，降低身体的紧张感，大脑就会自然而然地告诉你“没事，一切正常”。

turns.speaker: Jonny Miller
turns.en: Yeah. And maybe something that we haven't touched on yet, but I think is important to add in is this idea of interoception or somatic awareness. And the reason I bring it in is because if you do this practice but you're not really aware of your body and how you feel, then it'll be less compelling to you. But if you're kind of tuned into like sensations in your body, what's going on, you're more likely to notice the difference in the shifts.
turns.zh: 是的。可能还有个我们还没深入探讨但很重要的概念——内感知或躯体觉知。我之所以提到这个，是因为如果你只做练习却不真正关注身体的感觉和状态，那么这种练习对你的吸引力就会大打折扣。但如果你能专注于身体的感觉，留意身体的变化，就更有可能察觉到情绪的微妙转变。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Great. So let's get into that. That was something I definitely wanted to touch on here. This awesome acronym to help you with this process of interoception. So talk about what that is and then how to actually go about becoming better at being aware of what your body's doing.
turns.zh: 好的。那我们就深入探讨一下。这正是我想在这里重点讲的。这个帮助提升内感知能力的绝佳缩写词。请解释一下什么是内感知，以及如何通过训练提高对身体状态的感知能力。

turns.speaker: Jonny Miller
turns.en: Yeah. So it's this idea of interoception, which is known as our sixth sense, and basically it's our ability to sense, track and feel our internal landscape. And I like to use the metaphor of a chef in the same way that you train your flavor palette for kind of sweet, spicy, umami, things like that. You can also train your interoceptive palette and become more aware of the internal sensations, whether that's your breath, whether it's tension, whether it's moods and emotions, whether it's the quality of your awareness, the quality of your thoughts. And the more kind of in tune with that you are, the more likely you are to notice the kind of early warning signs of something like anxiety. Because usually, certainly a panic attack doesn't come out of nowhere. There will be a kind of cascade of subtle things that happen in your body that eventually result in anxiety. And so if you can catch those things early and kind of nip them in the bud and do one of these practices, then you can avoid the kind of 10 out of 10 worst case scenarios.
turns.zh: 是的。内感知被称为我们的第六感，本质上是感知、追踪和体验身体内部状态的能力。我喜欢用厨师训练味觉的比喻来类比——就像训练对甜、辣、鲜味等口味的敏感度一样，你也可以训练内感知能力，提高对身体内部感觉的觉知，无论是呼吸、紧张感、情绪波动，还是意识和思维的质量。越能与这些感觉保持同步，就越容易察觉焦虑等问题的早期预警信号。因为通常，恐慌发作并非突如其来。身体会出现一系列微妙变化，最终导致焦虑。所以如果能尽早发现这些信号，及时采取应对措施，比如进行这些呼吸练习，就能避免最糟糕的情况发生。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Okay, awesome. So I know that there's also specific things you recommend people pay attention to, to understand what their body is doing in this process of inter...
turns.zh: 好的，太棒了。我知道你还建议人们在内感知过程中特别注意一些细节，以理解身体的反应。

turns.speaker: Jonny Miller
turns.en: Interoception, yeah,
turns.zh: 内感知，对。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Interra... Okay. What is it?
turns.zh: 内感知……好吧。那是什么？

turns.speaker: Jonny Miller
turns.en: Interoception.
turns.zh: 内感知。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Interoception.
turns.zh: 内感知。

turns.speaker: Jonny Miller
turns.en: As opposed to exteroception, which is awareness of all the external stimuli.
turns.zh: 与外部感知不同，外部感知是对所有外部刺激的感知。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Got it. I guess before we even get to that, so you mentioned that it's another sense we have, and I think that's a really important point that I think maybe people didn't catch. So we have these five senses, obviously taste and smell and vision and touch. But you're finding and research showed basically this is another sense people don't really know we have.
turns.zh: 明白了。我觉得在深入探讨之前，你提到这是一种我们拥有的另一种感知方式，我认为这是一个非常重要的观点，也许很多人没有意识到。我们有五种感官，显然包括味觉、嗅觉、视觉和触觉。但你发现并通过研究证明，人们并不知道我们还有另一种感知方式。

turns.speaker: Jonny Miller
turns.en: Yeah, exactly. And it has been studies quite a lot, especially in the last decade or so. And there's a number of interesting findings from the research that I found. One being that ADHD tends to correlate with low levels of interoception, as does if people have PTSD or trauma. Again, interoception is lowered. And I'd certainly say for myself, for the first 25 years of my life, I was fairly numb from the neck down. I was not very aware to what was happening in my body in real time. I was also reading a book recently called The Hour Between Dog and Wolf, which looked at Wall Street traders and they correlated higher degrees of interception with basically making more money and making better decisions. And I think the thesis was that by tuning into what their body was doing in certain moments, they could pick up on things more intuitive decision making essentially.
turns.zh: 是的，确实如此。这项研究已经开展了很多年，尤其是在过去十年左右。研究得出了一些有趣的发现。其中之一是，注意力缺失症（ADHD）往往与低水平的内感知相关，创伤后应激障碍（PTSD）或创伤患者的情况也是如此。同样，内感知会降低。就我个人而言，在我生命的前25年里，我从颈部以下几乎没有任何感觉。我对身体实时发生的事情知之甚少。我最近读了一本叫《狗与狼之间的时刻》的书，书中研究了华尔街交易员，他们发现较高水平的内感知与赚更多钱和做出更明智决策之间存在关联。作者认为，通过关注身体在特定时刻的反应，交易员能够更直观地做出决策。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: So I think there's a specific list of things that you recommend people pay attention to, their posture, their breath, things like that. What is that list and then how do we actually do this better?
turns.zh: 所以我认为你建议人们关注的具体事项包括姿势、呼吸等。这份清单是什么？我们又该如何更好地做到这些呢？

turns.speaker: Jonny Miller
turns.en: Yeah. So I simplify this to APE, which basically is an acronym which stands for awareness, posture, and emotion. So to kind of go through each one by one. Awareness is, to give an example, I could narrow my awareness and become really focused and just you kind of tense up and it also is quite activating sometimes or you can relax and expand your awareness and be aware of the space above me, the space behind me, the space below me. And that is generally a calming thing. Posture is fairly self-explanatory. But again, our posture affects how we feel. You're shifting there now. And then emotion, which I include somatic or body-based sensations which arise. So both kind of what is the overall mood and the flavor or the texture that I'm feeling. Like right now, maybe it's excitement, maybe there's some joy. I'm noticing there's some heat in my belly probably from the breathing. Yeah, there's a little bit of tightness in my lower back from working out yesterday. So just sense kind of mapping that landscape of sensation. And for most people it's almost like it's like a [inaudible 00:30:22]. You have those maps of [inaudible 00:30:25] and for a lot of people there's just these big kind blind spots in their body.
turns.zh: 是的。我把它简化为APE，即觉察（Awareness）、姿势（Posture）和情绪（Emotion）的缩写。接下来逐一讲解。觉察方面，举个例子，我可以收窄注意力，变得非常专注，这时身体会变得紧张，有时也会激发动力；或者放松并扩展注意力，感知上方、下方和后方的空间，这通常能让人平静下来。姿势不言自明，但姿势确实影响情绪。你现在正在调整姿势。情绪方面，我把它包括基于身体的感觉，比如整体情绪和感觉到的质感或层次。比如现在，我可能感到兴奋，可能还有些快乐。我注意到腹部有热感，这可能来自呼吸。还有昨天锻炼后下背部有些紧绷。总之，就是感知这种感觉的地图。对于大多数人来说，这就像一张[00:30:22不可听清]地图。你有这些地图[00:30:25不可听清]，但很多人身体上有很多盲区。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: And the advice here is, so there's this acronym APE and the advice is think about these three things when you're feeling something that you may not, basically something's going on slash just often come back to this. I imagine just whenever you can think of, "Oh, APE: awareness, posture, emotion." Is that how to use this?
turns.zh: 这里的建议是，使用APE这个缩写，当你感觉到一些可能未被察觉的东西时，或者经常回归到这三个方面。我想只要你能想到“APE：觉察、姿势、情绪”，就可以这样用，对吧？

turns.speaker: Jonny Miller
turns.en: Yeah, exactly. So again, it can be something that you do before you start your day, maybe with a cup of tea. I like to drink tea and just do a body scan essentially and just check each of those three areas. And it's really valuable, particularly if you are having racing thoughts or something doesn't feel quite right. Instead of just tackling the problem on the level of the mind dropping down into the body and bringing that into the picture as well, I find to be really helpful.
turns.zh: 是的，没错。所以再说一次，你可以把这当作每天开始前要做的事，或许可以先喝杯茶。我喜欢喝茶，然后进行身体扫描，检查这三个方面。这真的很有价值，尤其是当你思绪纷乱，或是感觉有些不对劲的时候。与其只在头脑层面解决问题，不如将身体也纳入关注范围，我发现这真的很有帮助。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Basically, as often as you can. And generally when things are feeling all off, just remember APE, where's my awareness? How's my posture? And then what am I feeling? Am I feeling sad? Am I feeling happy, excited, angry? Things like that. I think you also talk about breath, like you have a list you wrote about this of other things that you might want to pay attention to. Actually finding paying attention to what my breath is doing is really powerful too. So I'm going to try a BAPE version of this or I'm going to try to think about where's my breath coming from, what am I feeling there?
turns.zh: 基本上是越频繁越好。如果感觉一切都乱了套，就记住APE法则——我的意识在哪里？我的姿势如何？然后我有什么感受？是悲伤？还是快乐、兴奋、愤怒？诸如此类。我想你还提到了呼吸，比如你写的清单上还有其他需要关注的方面。真正留意呼吸的变化也很有力。我打算尝试BAPE版本，或者思考呼吸从何处而来，此时我又有何种感受？

turns.speaker: Jonny Miller
turns.en: Yeah. So the breath and sensations are two other ones that are really helpful. The breath in particular, often people will... There's an idea of email apnea when people are checking their emails, they will, without noticing it, start to hold their breath, which is generally a very activating thing to do. Or as I mentioned earlier, if your breath is through the mouth and shallow and into the upper chest, that will also be very activating versus is your breath through the nose? Is it kind of into the belly and into the sides of the rib cage and does it feel easeful? Basically, breathing without tension is ideal.
turns.zh: 是的。呼吸和身体感受是另外两个很有用的方面。特别是呼吸，很多人在处理邮件时会不知不觉屏住呼吸，这其实很耗费精力。正如我之前提到的，如果呼吸通过口腔进行，且呼吸浅短，集中在上胸部，这同样会让人很紧张。而通过鼻腔呼吸，呼吸深入腹部，扩展到肋骨两侧，感觉会更加顺畅。基本上，没有紧张感的呼吸才是理想状态。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: What I think about using this practice is if I were sitting in a meeting and just not feeling amazingly confident, I just come back to this acronym, BAPE or APE, whichever one you want to choose, just like how am I feeling right now? Oh wow, my whole stomach is clenched. I'm maybe nervous about what might happen or I'm not breathing at all, or my posture is really bad. So I think in a meeting would be really helpful Here, maybe you're about to get on a zoom or an important call or something like that. Maybe a one-on-one. Is there anything else, any other moments that kind of triggers for people of like, "Oh, I should really be aware of what's happening right now. Let me do an APE exercise."
turns.zh: 我认为这种练习的应用场景是，如果我坐在会议中，感觉不是特别自信，我就会回想这个缩写词BAPE或APE，随便选一个，问问自己现在感觉如何？哦，天哪，我的整个胃都紧绷了。可能是对即将发生的事情感到紧张，或者根本不呼吸了，或者姿势很糟糕。所以在会议中运用这个方法会很有帮助。比如，你即将参加一个Zoom会议或重要通话，或是一对一交流。还有其他时刻会触发人们的警觉，比如“哦，我真的应该留意现在发生的事情。让我做个APE练习。”

turns.speaker: Jonny Miller
turns.en: Yeah, well, just to kind of piggyback on what you just said, if you are about to jump on a meeting and you're noticing that your stomach is clenched, that's actually really useful data to be like, "Why is this happening?" Is it your intuition kind of saying that maybe you shouldn't do this deal with someone or maybe something is off and so it's a sign to explore that more. Or it could be that you've been triggered by something or something that someone said and you've only just realized it and then that's again, more information or something that you can reflect on or go into.
turns.zh: 是的，嗯，接着你刚刚说的，如果你即将参加会议，发现胃紧绷，这其实是个很有用的信号，可以问问自己，“为什么会这样？”是你的直觉在提示你或许不该和某人达成交易？还是有些事情不对劲？这都是值得深思的信号。或者可能是被某个人的话激怒了，而你刚刚才意识到。这又提供了更多信息，或是值得反思的素材。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Is there anything in your life recently that is an example of this where you're feeling unsure and maybe you realize, "Oh, here's what my body's doing, maybe I should pay more attention to this."
turns.zh: 最近你生活中有没有这样的例子？你感到不确定，然后意识到，“哦，原来我的身体在这样反应，或许我该多关注一下。”

turns.speaker: Jonny Miller
turns.en: Actually, last week I did a podcast conversation, so I have a podcast myself, and I got off the call and I remember I felt or got off the podcast and I felt pretty exhausted and I felt like there was this kind of tension in my chest. And again, my breath was kind of all over the place and I realized that I had very much over committed myself for that week. I'd scheduled back to back podcast interviews. The podcast wasn't even the priority for what I'm focusing on in this quarter, so I then made the decision to just push back all my episodes until the summer basically.
turns.zh: 实际上，我上周参加了一次播客访谈，所以我自己也做了一档播客。结束通话后，我记得当时感觉非常疲惫，胸口还有种压抑感。再说，我的呼吸也相当不稳定，这时我才意识到那一周自己把自己安排得太满了。我安排了接连不断的播客采访，而播客甚至都不是我本季度关注的重点。因此，我决定把所有播客节目推迟到夏天再进行。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: I love that example. I know that feeling very well.
turns.zh: 我很喜欢这个例子。我深有同感。

turns.speaker: Jonny Miller
turns.en: I'm sure.
turns.zh: 我确定。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: When you wrote about this idea of interoception, you connected it to burnout, and I think you talked about how this is one of the best tools to avoid burnout. Is that right? Am I remembering that right? And if so, how do you think about this burnout and avoiding burnout in general, something a lot of people experience?
turns.zh: 你写到内感知这个概念时，将其与职业倦怠联系起来，我记得你曾说这是避免职业倦怠的最佳工具之一。是这样吗？我没记错吧？如果是这样的话，你如何看待职业倦怠和避免职业倦怠这件事？毕竟这是很多人都会经历的。

turns.speaker: Jonny Miller
turns.en: Yeah, so I have this idea that I call the feather brick dump truck phenomenon. And basically what that means is when we are showing early signs of burnout, our body will give us feedback usually in subtle ways in the beginning. So the feather might be waking up in the morning and feeling a little bit tired, maybe a little bit exhausted. The brick, maybe you ignore that or you don't notice it, and then three or four weeks later you have a fight with someone or an argument or you just feel frustrated and terrible and you lose your cool. And then maybe the dump truck is a month later or even a year later, there's a full-blown health crisis, or you develop type two diabetes or there's a whole range of things, or maybe you get fired. There's a bunch of different things that can happen, but normally depending on how attuned or depending on someone's interoceptive capacity, ideally, you want to notice when it's the feather and then make adjustments or shift then and not have to wait until you experience the full-blown pain of the dump truck, which unfortunately is what happens to a lot of people, especially when they experience burnout for the first time.
turns.zh: 是的，我有个概念叫“羽毛—砖块—自卸卡车现象”。简单来说，当我们出现职业倦怠的早期迹象时，身体通常会以微妙的方式给我们反馈。比如“羽毛”可能是早上醒来时感觉有点疲倦、有些许精疲力竭。“砖块”可能是你忽视了这些反馈，或者没有注意到它们。三四周后，你可能会和某人发生争执、吵架，或者感到沮丧、情绪崩溃，甚至失去冷静。一个月或一年后，可能就会爆发健康危机，比如患上二型糖尿病，或者出现一系列其他问题，甚至被解雇。这些情况都有可能发生，但通常取决于一个人的内感知能力。如果能及早察觉“羽毛”的信号，就能及时调整和改变策略，而不必等到自卸卡车彻底碾压过来，很遗憾，很多人就是这样，尤其是那些初次经历职业倦怠的人。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: This is such an important point and such a good way of thinking about it.
